newsitem.title: BELARUS: RJ Reynolds -Belarus tobacco deal off.
newsitem.headline: RJ Reynolds -Belarus tobacco deal off.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko has vetoed a potential deal with R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co to form a joint venture with the Grodno tobacco factory to produce cigarettes.

"Why should I sell it (Grodno) when the fruits of such a company's labour are a central source of revenue to national budgets the world over," Lukashenko said during a political rally on Sunday night.
Grodno, which produces 11 billion cigarettes a year, is operating at half-capacity.
Lukashenko said he told Reynolds, a unit of U.S. consumer goods group RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, to invest in Belarus truck manufacturers and electronics.
"But what I want, they don't want," he said.
Reynolds began talks with the Belarussian government in 1994 to upgrade Grodno and bring production of cigarettes, including Reynolds's Camel brand, to 18 billion annually.

"Starting capital for the project would have been no less than $20 million, with 50 percent of shares going to Belarus and the other 50 percent going to Reynolds," an official from the Ministry of Foreign Economic Relations told Reuters.
Government officials said previously that workers' groups were opposed to the deal and had appealed about it to the president.
